newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer hopes mark correction doesn't go too far.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer hopes mark correction doesn't go too far.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said on Thursday he hoped the correction of the mark against the dollar would not go too far.
Tietmeyer, speaking to Spanish journalists in Frankfurt, also said in an interview that he was watching foreign exchange market developments "very closely".
A recorded audio tape of the interview was made available to Reuters.
"For the most part exchange rate developments are the result of corrections which were necessary. I hope now that it will not come to an overreaction," Tietmeyer said.
"We are watching developments very carefully," he said.

At a Bundesbank news conference last week, Tietmeyer said the mark's correction against the U.S. currency was complete and it was important for the mark to be strong ahead of Germany's entry into European economic and monetary union (EMU)
The mark, which hit its lowest point for almost six years against the dollar on Tuesday, was slightly more healthy on Thursday and was trading at about 1.79 marks in late European dealings.
